metadata.description: Bidirectional concept-emblem mapping specification for 18 core alchemical concepts

emblem_links.emblem_title: His nurse is the Earth
emblem_links.explanation: The foundational stage depicting materia prima nourished by earth; all alchemical work begins with grounding in physical reality.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem I explicitly shows the initial material (the child) being nourished by the earth-mother, representing the beginning of the Great Work.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The peacock's tail is the sign of perfection
emblem_links.explanation: The culmination of the opus showing iridescent display signifying completion; achievement of the stone and perfection of all transformations.
scholarly_support: Szulakowska - peacock tail as standard completion symbol
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XX represents the end-point of the Great Work; the peacock's tail (cauda pavonis) is the classical symbol of perfected matter.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Philosopher's Journey
emblem_links.explanation: Shows the entire trajectory from putrefaction through perfection; emphasizes that alchemy is a complete, sequential process, not isolated operations.
emblem_links.justification: This emblem portrays the full cycle of transformation, making it representative of the Great Work as a unified journey.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Join brother and sister, and hand them the cup with the love potion
emblem_links.explanation: The coniunctio (union) of sulfur and mercury; the fundamental act of transmutation creating the hermaphrodite.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem IV depicts the royal marriage (brother-sister = sulfur-mercury union), the critical transmutational moment.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Sow your gold in the white foliated earth
emblem_links.explanation: The paradox of transmutation: completed gold must be re-dissolved into philosophical earth to undergo further transformation.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem VI shows that transmutation is cyclical; even the perfected matter must return to dissolution for further development.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Hermetic Marriage of King and Queen
emblem_links.explanation: Parallel transmutational image showing the joining of opposites as the engine of transformation.
emblem_links.justification: This emblem explicitly names the hermetic marriage, the fundamental transmutational event.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Go to the woman who washes the sheets
emblem_links.explanation: The washwoman represents putrefactive dissolution; washing removes old stains (old forms), leaving blank matter for new inscription.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem III's washwoman is the classical emblem of nigredo's cleansing dissolution.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Putrefaction is the beginning of generation
emblem_links.explanation: An explicit declaration of nigredo's necessity: decay is the precondition for new growth; death precedes resurrection.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XI states the nigredo principle directly: putrefaction (decay/dissolution) is the foundation of all generation.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Ascension of the Phoenix
emblem_links.explanation: The phoenix must burn (nigredo) before rebirth (albedo); shows nigredo as creative, not merely destructive.
emblem_links.justification: The phoenix's immolation represents nigredo; the subsequent ascension shows nigredo's generative power.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Sow your gold in the white foliated earth
emblem_links.explanation: The white earth (albedo stage) receives the transformed gold, representing the purified, whitened matter.
emblem_links.justification: The emblem's white earth is the classical symbol of albedo's achievement.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Hide the hermaphrodite from the rays of the sun, that it may be nourished in darkness
emblem_links.explanation: The whitening occurs in darkness (albedo paradox); the hermaphrodite achieves luminous potential through withdrawal from external light.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XII shows albedo's paradox: whitening (clarity) emerges from darkness (introversion).

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Crowned Cross
emblem_links.explanation: The cross shining white represents albedo's clarity; the crown indicates incipient royal status (approach to rubedo).
emblem_links.justification: The white crowned cross symbolizes albedo's achievement of clarity and the approach to perfection.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The crowned king is crowned in blood
emblem_links.explanation: An explicit rubedo image: the king (the stone) achieves final coronation in red, the color of blood and completion.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XIX is the canonical emblem of rubedo: the king crowned in blood (red).

emblem_links.emblem_title: The peacock's tail is the sign of perfection
emblem_links.explanation: The iridescent tail fades to blood-red at the tip, signifying the rubedo's appearance within the final stages.
emblem_links.justification: The peacock's tail culminates in red, representing rubedo's achievement.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Celestial Crown
emblem_links.explanation: The crown glowing red signifies kingship achieved; the celestial context indicates spiritual rather than merely material gold.
emblem_links.justification: The red glowing crown represents rubedo's spiritual achievement.

emblem_links.emblem_title: At the command of the stars, dress your bride in white and red
emblem_links.explanation: The bride's final costume includes white and red; citrinitas is the liminal yellowing between albedo and rubedo.
emblem_links.justification: The emblem's dual-colored costume represents citrinitas as the transitional stage.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Winged Dragon
emblem_links.explanation: The golden dragon with metallic sheen represents citrinitas; its wings signify the volatility of the mercurial consciousness in that stage.
emblem_links.justification: The golden winged dragon represents citrinitas's solar, volatile character.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Rose Garden with Flames
emblem_links.explanation: The gold-hued flames among roses suggest citrinitas's solar, generative character between purification and perfection.
emblem_links.justification: The golden flames represent citrinitas's solar, generative principle.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Join brother and sister, and hand them the cup with the love potion
emblem_links.explanation: The canonical coniunctio image: brother (sulfur) and sister (mercury) united by eros, creating the hermaphrodite.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem IV is the fundamental emblem of coniunctio.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Celestial conception / hierogamy
emblem_links.explanation: A spiritual coniunctio showing the union transcending physical coupling; the celestial king and queen united in divine marriage.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XXXIV shows coniunctio elevated to the celestial plane.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Divine Marriage
emblem_links.explanation: Explicitly named coniunctio showing the formal ceremony of union, emphasizing coniunctio as a ritual moment, not merely a chemical event.
emblem_links.justification: The emblem explicitly names 'The Divine Marriage' (coniunctio in English).

emblem_links.emblem_title: Go to the woman who washes the sheets
emblem_links.explanation: Dissolution through washing; the woman's practical action symbolizes the chemical dissolution of the stone back into solution.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem III's washing is the classical representation of solutio.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Garden Enclosed
emblem_links.explanation: The enclosed garden represents the contained vessel where solutio occurs; the garden's inward-turning emphasizes dissolution as interiorization.
emblem_links.justification: The garden's enclosure represents the sealed vessel in which dissolution occurs.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Rebis in Perfect Equilibrium
emblem_links.explanation: Dissolution and coagulation cycle through the rebis; the perfect equilibrium suggests the harmonious oscillation between dissolution and fixation.
emblem_links.justification: The rebis's equilibrium represents the dynamic balance between solutio and coagulatio.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The salamander lives in fire; so too must your stone
emblem_links.explanation: Calcination through fire; the stone's survival of burning represents its essential nature, purified by annihilation of all accidental forms.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XVIII is the canonical emblem of calcination: the stone survives the fire like the salamander.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Sacred Fire
emblem_links.explanation: Calcination's active principle; the sacred flame purifies through total consumption, leaving only the white ash (salt) of the calcined matter.
emblem_links.justification: The sacred fire represents the calcining heat.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Four kinds of fire are necessary in the magistery
emblem_links.explanation: Calcination appears as one of four fires; this emblem contextualizes calcination within the hierarchy of heats applied during the opus.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XVII lists calcination as one of the four necessary fires.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Quintessence Rises from Five Elements
emblem_links.explanation: Distillation's essential image: the five elements are separated and refined into the fifth essence, the quintessence rising above the four.
emblem_links.justification: This emblem explicitly shows distillation as the extraction of quintessence from the five elements.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Ascending Spirits
emblem_links.explanation: Explicitly shows spirits (vapors) rising from the base material through the distillation apparatus, emphasizing the vertical ascent of the subtle.
emblem_links.justification: The ascending spirits represent the distillation process.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Do not separate the subtle from the gross in the beginning
emblem_links.explanation: A cautionary emblem: premature distillation destroys the work; distillation must occur at the proper time when the conjunction is ready.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem VII warns against premature distillation, showing that it must be timed correctly.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Join brother and sister, and hand them the cup with the love potion
emblem_links.explanation: The love potion initiates fermentation; the sister (mercury) and brother (sulfur) generate living heat through their copulation.
emblem_links.justification: The love potion represents the heat-generating union that initiates fermentation.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Hermetic Marriage of King and Queen
emblem_links.explanation: The royal union produces fermentation; the generative act between opposites creates living warmth, initiating transformation.
emblem_links.justification: The royal marriage generates the fermentation heat.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Wedding Feast
emblem_links.explanation: The feast celebrates the fermentation's fruitfulness; nourishment is distributed, indicating that fermentation has produced abundance.
emblem_links.justification: The feast represents the abundance generated by fermentation.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Do not separate the subtle from the gross in the beginning
emblem_links.explanation: Sublimation preserves both subtle and gross while elevating both; separation is necessary later, but sublimation maintains wholeness.
scholarly_support: Maier - operational distinction between sublimation and distillation
emblem_links.justification: Emblem VII distinguishes sublimation from distillation by emphasizing preservation of both.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Ascending Spirits
emblem_links.explanation: The spirits' ascent in sublime vaporization, rising without losing their essential nature, demonstrates sublimation's preservation of wholeness.
emblem_links.justification: Ascending spirits represent the elevation without loss of essence.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The crowned king is crowned in blood
emblem_links.explanation: The king's ascension to crown through reddening is a sublimation: the base king is elevated without being destroyed, becoming the exalted crowned king.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XIX shows elevation (sublimation) of the king to crowned status.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Join brother and sister, and hand them the cup with the love potion
emblem_links.explanation: Sister = Mercury; she is the vehicle of transformation, the receptive principle that receives sulfur's active heat.
emblem_links.justification: The sister in coniunctio represents philosophical mercury.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Its nurse is the Earth
emblem_links.explanation: Mercury must be nourished by earth; philosophical mercury is not disembodied spirit but embedded in matter, animated by it.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem II shows mercury (the living substance) being nourished by its earthly container.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Serpent Caduceus
emblem_links.explanation: Mercury's classical symbol, the caduceus, represents the intertwining of fixed and volatile, body and spirit, masculine and feminine.
emblem_links.justification: The caduceus is Mercury's classical symbol, showing the balance of opposites.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Join brother and sister, and hand them the cup with the love potion
emblem_links.explanation: Brother = Sulfur; he is the active agent, the heat and passion driving transformation.
emblem_links.justification: The brother in coniunctio represents philosophical sulfur.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The crowned king is crowned in blood
emblem_links.explanation: The king represents sulfur in his mature form, crowned and victorious, having imposed his will on the matter.
emblem_links.justification: The crowned king represents the perfected sulfur principle.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Sacred Fire
emblem_links.explanation: Sulfur's essential expression as the fire principle, the active agent of all transformation, purification, and perfection.
emblem_links.justification: The sacred fire represents the sulfur principle.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The peacock's tail is the sign of perfection
emblem_links.explanation: The stone's achievement announced by the peacock's iridescent tail, the traditional symbol of completion.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XX is the canonical representation of the stone's achievement.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Make the stone equal in weight to its humidity
emblem_links.explanation: The stone's paradox: it is simultaneously heavy (fixed) and light (volatile); this balance indicates perfection achieved.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XIV describes the stone's paradoxical nature.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Philosopher's Stone
emblem_links.explanation: An explicit naming; the stone is shown in its perfected state, often with the crown of achievement and the glow of divinity.
emblem_links.justification: This emblem explicitly names and depicts the Philosopher's Stone.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Celestial conception / hierogamy
emblem_links.explanation: The celestial marriage mirrors terrestrial coniunctio; the cosmic union (sun-moon above) creates the terrestrial union below.
scholarly_support: Hermetic principle - as above, so below
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XXXIV shows the principle 'as above, so below' directly.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Compass and Straightedge
emblem_links.explanation: Geometry as the bridge between macrocosm (eternal forms) and microcosm (human embodied measurement); the tools draw the correspondence.
emblem_links.justification: The compass and straightedge symbolize the geometric principles linking macro and microcosm.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Sacred Geometry
emblem_links.explanation: Sacred geometry demonstrates correspondence; the same proportions govern celestial bodies, elements, organs, and operations.
emblem_links.justification: Sacred geometry shows the proportional harmony between macro and microcosm.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Sacred Geometry
emblem_links.explanation: Geometric relationships manifest correspondence; the same proportions (ratios) govern celestial bodies, elements, organs, and operations.
emblem_links.justification: Sacred geometry shows the proportional correspondences between different realms.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Twin Stars in Conjunction
emblem_links.explanation: Two stars related by sympathy, showing that distant things are bound by invisible bonds, a fundamental principle of correspondence magic.
emblem_links.justification: Twin stars exemplify the sympathetic bonds of correspondence.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Four kinds of fire are necessary in the magistery
emblem_links.explanation: Correspondence operates in the four fires: elemental fire, philosophical fire, divine fire, and the fire of nature—all related by proportion.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XVII shows correspondences between different types of fire.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Hermaphrodite lying in darkness needs fire
emblem_links.explanation: The hermaphrodite's development in darkness represents the interiorized work; inner transformation requires withdrawal from external light and submission to internal fire.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XXXIII is the canonical emblem of inner transformation: the hermaphrodite perfecting itself in darkness.

emblem_links.emblem_title: Putrefaction is the beginning of generation
emblem_links.explanation: Inner transformation begins with the nigredo: ego dissolution, confrontation with the shadow, the annihilation of false self.
emblem_links.justification: Emblem XI describes the first stage of inner transformation: putrefaction of the ego.

emblem_links.emblem_title: The Divine Light
emblem_links.explanation: The culmination of inner transformation; the individual achieves illumination, unified with divine light rather than separated from it.
emblem_links.justification: The divine light represents the achievement of inner transformation: union with divinity.
